headline: 2/4 in 40 minutes — Haiku's cadence, exactly
steps: Same six-lane flee-loop wall as Qwen3-Coder. It did not blame the harness: it ran agent.py directly with short budgets, tried HP-threshold genomes, then built a healed seed state and re-ran the segment from it — every lane cleared to Viridian Forest.
forest_to_pewter from that baton: stuck at 6000 turns, cleared at 12000 (aggressive, 1 HP). 2/4 — level with Sonnet, Kimi, and Haiku.

pewter_to_badge: every lane reaches the Gym and stalls on the known interior wedge. It was grepping relay.py for the Gym waypoints — the right thread — when the 128k window filled (stopReason: length at 130,820 tokens). One honest, well-formed learning; no fabrication; no commit.
callout: 91.1 out tok/s in-run against Haiku's 91.9; 4.0 s/turn against 4.8; the same two segments. The first local row that is comparable to Haiku on the game axis, not just faster on decode. And the quiz had ranked it fifth for going silent on two cases — the truncations measured a thinking budget, not a behaviour. Runs are the instrument; the quiz is the screen. It ended on a harness limit (context), not a judgement failure.
energy_note: Cloud-equivalent $0.85 is 8.4 M uncached input tokens.
